code: # Construct a Poisson( 1 ) random variable Pois_RV <- distribution.poisson( lambda = 1 )  # Evaluate the density, equivalent to dpois( 0 : 5, lambda = 1 ) Pois_RV$d( 0 : 5 ) #> [1] 0.367879441 0.367879441 0.183939721 0.061313240 0.015328310 0.003065662  # Evaluate the distribution function, equivalent to ppois( 0 : 5, lambda = 1 ) Pois_RV$p( 0 : 5 ) #> [1] 0.3678794 0.7357589 0.9196986 0.9810118 0.9963402 0.9994058  # Evaluate the quantile function, equivalent to qpois( c( 0.5, 0.8 ), lambda = 1 ) Pois_RV$q( c( 0.5, 0.8 ) ) #> [1] 1 2  # Generate random deviates, equivalent to rpois( 10, lambda = 1 ) Pois_RV$r( 10 ) #>  [1] 0 2 1 0 0 1 1 0 1 2  # Update parameters to a Poisson( 10 ) random variable Pois_RV$params <- list( lambda = 10 ) mean( Pois_RV$r( 1e5 ) ) #> [1] 9.99972

title: Checks a variable is a single number (and optionally, in a range and not NA) — check_numeric
code: # These are all OK: check_numeric(0) check_numeric(0L) check_numeric(0, lower = 0) check_numeric(0, upper = 0) check_numeric(NA_real_, allow_missing = TRUE) check_numeric(Inf) check_numeric(-Inf) # These return errors: try(check_numeric("foo")) #> Error in check_numeric("foo") : is.numeric(x) is not TRUE try(check_numeric(1:2)) #> Error in check_numeric(1:2) : length(x) == 1 is not TRUE try(check_numeric(NA_real_)) #> Error in check_numeric(NA_real_) : !is.na(x) is not TRUE try(check_numeric(NA, allow_missing = TRUE)) # NA is logical, not numeric #> Error in check_numeric(NA, allow_missing = TRUE) :  #>   is.numeric(x) is not TRUE try(check_numeric(0, lower = 1)) #> Error in check_numeric(0, lower = 1) : x >= lower is not TRUE try(check_numeric(0, lower = 0, lower_inclusive = FALSE)) #> Error in check_numeric(0, lower = 0, lower_inclusive = FALSE) :  #>   x > lower is not TRUE

title: Plots the marginal posteriors of each parameter in a stanfit object — plot_posterior
text: posterior_samples stanfit object e.g. returned rstan::sampling(). contain samples posterior. prior_samples stanfit object containing samples prior, prior posterior distributions overlaid. default value NA means posterior plotted. true_param_values named numeric vector: names parameters, values true values (known simulation truth). Using argument means output plot include vertical lines true values. default value NA means lines included. params_desired character vector parameter names. Using argument means named parameters included plot. default value NA means parameters included. transforms named list functions, names parameter names. Using argument means parameter named list transformed applying associated function sampled values plotting. e.g. specifying list(x=log) result log function applied values parameter "x". Note names parameters appear plot updated reflect functions applied, therefore argument usually used together labels argument. default value NA means transforms applied parameter. labels named character vector, names names parameters named within stanfit object, values new names use instead. e.g. transforms=list(x=log) specified, labels=c(x="log(x))" make sense, label plot posterior x reflects log transformation. lower lower value x axis one params. sampled values less lower increased exactly equal lower, left-bin histogram occur lower contain overflow. Use arg specify either single value used params, named numeric vector whose names params. upper upper value x axis one params. sampled values greater upper decreased exactly equal upper, right-bin histogram occur upper contain overflow. Use arg specify either single value used params, named numeric vector whose names params. nrow, ncol Number rows columns individual plots parameter arranged grid. Passed ggplot2::facet_wrap(). skip_stanfit_to_dt argument set TRUE, posterior_samples argument (prior_samples argument used) used provide datatable samples instead stanfit object samples, example already run stanfit_to_dt() stanfit objects. allows e.g. manual renaming parameters plotting. bins positive integer number bins, passed ggplot2::geom_histogram(). default 30.

code: simulate_mixture_of_two_normals(   n = 500,   groups = LETTERS[1:5],   group_frequencies = rep(1/length(groups), length(groups)),   mu_0 = 0,   mu_1 = mu_0 + 3,   sd_0 = 0.5,   sd_1 = 1,   p = 0.5,   sd_groups = 1 )

title: Simulate (randomly draw) numbers from a mixture of two normal distributions. — simulate_mixture_of_two_normals
text: n non-negative integer: number observations simulate. groups character vector: set categories differ proportions mixture. Specify character(0) observations category, .e. observations probability coming one component mixture . group_frequencies numeric vector length groups, value frequency group (proportion 0 1). mu_0 number: smaller means two normals. mu_1 number: larger means two normals. sd_0 non-negative number: standard deviation normal mean mu_0. sd_1 non-negative number: standard deviation normal mean mu_1. p probability observation coming normal mean mu_1. sd_groups non-negative number: standard deviation normal variability regression coefficients groups (logit scale).

title: Simulate (randomly draw) numbers from a mixture of two normal distributions. — simulate_mixture_of_two_normals
text: dataframe n rows, one per observation. column y contains values drawn normal mixture. column d contains logical variable whether observation came normal mean mu_1.

title: Simulate (randomly draw) numbers from a mixture of two normal distributions. — simulate_mixture_of_two_normals
code: df <- simulate_mixture_of_two_normals()$data hist(df$y)  hist(df[df$d, ]$y)   # the normal with mean mu_1  hist(df[! df$d, ]$y) # the normal with mean mu_0
